Preliminary. Stratification now comes from the hydrography step (validated against the ship CTD), but epsilon QC, the noise floor and interface/layer classification are not final, so read the response to the controls rather than single values. The VMP5500 has no usable salinity below the ship CTD's 550 m reach.

Probe agreement after QC

What the QC choices change

From the baseline run (both instruments, all casts). Each finding can be reproduced with the controls.

Fixing the stratification moved the VMP5500 ratio from about 29 to 1.5

perturb's window-scale N² for the VMP5500 was about 4.5× too large and its dT/dz about 2.3× too small, and the shipboard archive carried the same values. The hydrography step now computes N² and Tz with TEOS-10, taking VMP5500 salinity from the nearest ship CTD's T–S relation because its conductivity cell is too noisy for gradients. Both instruments then match the ship CTD (N² median ratio 1.01 and 1.08, Rρ about 1.7). The pooled 150–550 m ratio of averages at the process station falls from 29 to 1.5 for the VMP5500 and from 4.3 to 3.5 for the VMP250. Select "perturb window values" to see the old answer.

The figure-of-merit cut is now the choice that matters most

With stratification fixed, the ATOMIX cut (FM above 1.15) doubles the VMP250's pooled ratio (3.5 to 6.8) and raises the VMP5500's (1.5 to 1.9), while removing about half the windows. It rejects 41–77% of windows in every epsilon decade, including high epsilon, which points to the threshold not suiting these spectra (4 s FFT, 16 s windows) rather than to bad data. Inspect spectra before adopting it.

Below about 200 m the ratios exceed 1 and bracket the finger prediction

In 25 m bins from 200 to 550 m the ratio ranges from about 1.3 to 10, against a salt-finger prediction of about 3–5 for γ = 0.65 at the observed Rρ of 1.5–2. Above 200 m the ratios are near 1. Restricting to finger-favourable windows (Turner 45–90°) changes little, because nearly all windows below 150 m already are. The fit scale matters less than expected: 5 to 25 m changes the pooled ratio by at most about 35% (VMP250 2.3–3.7, VMP5500 1.4–1.6).

The two instruments agree where both measure

At the process station between 150 and 250 m, median ε is 8.9×10⁻¹⁰ (VMP250 free fall) and 8.0×10⁻¹⁰ W kg⁻¹ (VMP5500); median χ is 3.9×10⁻⁸ and 3.7×10⁻⁸ K² s⁻¹. The VMP250 covers only the top 270 m, through 15 profiles, so its ratios rest on far fewer windows.

Their noise floors differ by a factor of ten

The lowest epsilon each instrument reports is about 3×10⁻¹⁰ (VMP250) and 3×10⁻¹¹ W kg⁻¹ (VMP5500). VMP250 epsilon below 150 m sits within about 2× of its floor, so treat it as near an upper bound, which makes its ratios lower bounds. Excluding below-floor windows biases means high; setting them to the floor barely moves anything here.

Segment QC matters little below 50 m

The proposed thresholds remove 4.4% of VMP250 and 2.3% of VMP5500 windows, mostly in the top 20 m, and change the 150–600 m mean ε by under 3%. Variance resolved never binds, and the probe-pair rule changes means by under 1%.
